Text:
# ASPERGILLUS SPECIES

For localized disease (fungus ball), antifungal therapy is ineffective.

Consult Surgery and Pulmonary for cases of localized disease without systemic infection. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat invasive disease with intravenous antifungals initially, then switch to oral antifungals for a total duration of therapy of 6-12 weeks dependent on the degree and duration of immunosuppression, site of disease and evidence of disease improvement.

References:

- Mandell Chapter: Aspergillus Species
- Patterson et al. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2016, 63(4): e1-60
- Sanford keyword: Aspergillosis, Invasive
- Up-to-Date article: Treatment and prevention of invasive aspergillosis
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Preferred intravenous therapy

Voriconazole 6 mg/kg IV q12h for 2 doses, then 4 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) R,H,

### Alternative intravenous therapy for patients intolerant to voriconazole

Liposomal amphotericin (Ambisome) 3-5 mg/kg IV q24h ($$$$) [R,O]

### Oral therapy after disease has stabilized

Voriconazole 200 mg PO q12h ($$) R,H,DI

## Outpatient

### Preferred intravenous therapy

Voriconazole 6 mg/kg IV q12h for 2 doses, then 4 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) R,H,

### Alternative intravenous therapy for patients intolerant to voriconazole

Amphotericin B Liposomal 3-5MG/KG IV q24h ($$$$)R,O+ NS Hydratio

### Oral therapy after disease has stabilized

Voriconazole 200 mg PO q12h ($$) R,H,DI
